text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Vandalism and neglect at the country's largest university has left the institution ill-equipped and dilapidated, the auditor-general said in a report.
- Over 3,000 squatters in the northern mining town of Kitwe say they will resist being moved to another area by Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) and the local authority.
- Defence minister Ben Mwila says the government is investigating reports that former president Kenneth Kaunda recently met with a South African arms firm boss.
- Deputy commerce minister Ackim Nkole says the state-run Zambia National Commercial Bank is to open a branch in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
- The anti-corruption commission says it is investigating local government and housing minister Ben Mwiinga for corruption.
- A British Airways spokesman says the strike by British Airways staff in London will affect the travel plans of some 350 Zambians.
